title: Felix and the Choir
premise: Tamsin Thackeray, the king's food-taster who has survived poison and knows every smuggler's pass through the Thornfell mountains, is handed a dying stranger's map — a key to the Choir, an ancient covenant between the human realms and the mountain's hidden fae courts that was shattered a generation ago. Hunted by the usurper Duke Corvane's inquisitors, she gathers a ragtag company of smugglers, exiles, and one disgraced court singer whose voice alone can reopen the covenant. As Corvane's armies march on the free cities, Tamsin must choose between loyalty to the crown that raised her and the truth that her own immunity was engineered to make her a living weapon against the fae. In the end she reforges the Choir at terrible cost — singing the covenant herself with poisoned blood as her instrument — breaking Corvane's hold and finding, at last, a family that chose her back.
about_author: Ivo Fairweather is the pen name of a former choir singer turned archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border folklore in remote mountain villages. Their fiction blends the textures of old ballads with the hard practicalities of people who live by their wits.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. In the royal kitchens, Tamsin tastes a suspect dish and survives what should have killed her, drawing the suspicion of the king's spymaster. Establishes her isolation, her trained senses, and the quiet dread of a life spent being poisoned on purpose. Emotional beat: competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Salt Gate
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. A bleeding stranger collapses at the city's salt gate, pressing a folded map into Tamsin's hands and whispering 'the Choir remembers' before dying. The spymaster arrives too late; Tamsin hides the map out of instinct rather than intent. Beat: fear and the first pull of destiny.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Alone in her garret, Tamsin studies the map: passes that don't exist, marked with musical notation instead of roads. An inquisitor knocks; she lies for the first time in her careful life. Beat: the point of no return, chosen in panic.

chapters.title: Down the Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Fleeing through Thornfell by routes only she knows, Tamsin evades pursuit but realizes someone inside the palace sold her name. She reaches the free city of Marrowgate seeking the map's first landmark. Beat: exhilaration curdling into exile.

chapters.title: The Disgraced Singer
chapters.summary: POV Merrin Vale. Introduce Merrin, once the court's finest voice, now singing in dockside taverns after refusing to perform at Corvane's ascension. He recognizes the notation on Tamsin's map as covenant-song. Beat: two broken people recognizing each other's damage.

chapters.title: Inquisitors in Marrowgate
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Corvane's inquisitors sweep the city; a tavern contact betrays them for coin. Merrin's street-smarts save them, and they escape downriver with a stolen boat and a growing mutual reliance. Beat: trust built under fire.

chapters.title: The Company of the Broken
chapters.summary: POV Merrin. They gather allies: Brannoc, a dwarf smuggler who owes Tamsin's father; Sef, a runaway fae-blooded child; and Old Wren, a hedge-witch who remembers the old rites. A found family begins to assemble around the map. Beat: warmth after flight.

chapters.title: Voices Under the Mountain
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Following the map's first notation, they hear faint harmonies from deep beneath Thornfell — the Choir still half-alive. Wren explains the covenant: song binding human and fae realms in mutual protection. Beat: wonder, and grief for what was lost.

chapters.title: Corvane's Proclamation
chapters.summary: POV Merrin. News spreads: Duke Corvane declares the free cities in rebellion and marches north. His inquisitors carry instruments designed to shatter fae-song. The stakes sharpen from personal survival to war. Beat: dread of the gathering storm.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse Ambush
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. At a mountain tollhouse, inquisitors ambush them. Tamsin's poison-trained body lets her survive a drugged blade meant to capture her alive — proof they want her specifically. First blood shed in their defense. Beat: guilt and resolve entwined.

chapters.title: Why They Want Me
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Wren examines Tamsin's scars and old taster's records: her immunity wasn't trained, it was brewed — her blood is toxic to fae. She was made a weapon before she could walk. Beat: betrayal by the crown that raised her.

chapters.title: Sef's Secret
chapters.summary: POV Sef. The child reveals they can hear the Choir clearly because they're fae-blooded — and that something below is calling them home. The group debates using Sef as a guide versus protecting them. Beat: the found family's first fracture over sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: POV Merrin. They reach the ruined underground hall where the covenant was sung. Empty thrones, dead acoustics, and carvings showing humans and fae singing as one. Merrin attempts the opening verse; the stone answers with silence. Beat: awe shadowed by despair.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Name
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Captured correspondence reveals who betrayed her at court: Master Aldous, the spymaster who taught her everything. Her mentor has been Corvane's all along. Beat: the wound of misplaced loyalty.

chapters.title: Winter Camp
chapters.summary: POV Brannoc. Snowbound in a smuggler's cave, the company shares stories — Tamsin's childhood of tasting, Merrin's silencing, Sef's flight. Bonds deepen; Tamsin realizes she has never had a family until now. Beat: quiet heart of the book.

chapters.title: The Fae Border
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. They cross into the twilight verge where the fae realm bleeds through. Time bends; Wren's wards strain. Tamsin's poisonous blood makes the land itself recoil from her. Beat: belonging and unbelonging in the same step.

chapters.title: Audience with the Ash Queen
chapters.summary: POV Merrin. The fae court receives them coldly: the last covenant broke when humans slaughtered the singers. The Ash Queen demands a price for alliance — the death of the one whose blood kills fae. Meaning Tamsin. Beat: horror of being the obstacle.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Tamsin refuses to die on command and argues her case: her blood can also carry the covenant, if sung through. The Queen grants a single chance — reforge the Choir at the Deepwell before the moon turns, or be hunted by both armies. Beat: defiance earning grudging respect.

chapters.title: Aldous Catches Up
chapters.summary: POV Aldous. The spymaster corners them at the verge's edge, offering Tamsin pardon if she surrenders the map. She sees the man who raised her clearly for the first time — and chooses the family beside her. Escape costs Wren a grave wound. Beat: loyalty tested and proven.

chapters.title: What Wren Knows
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Dying slowly, Wren teaches Tamsin the covenant's structure: it needs three voices — mortal, fae, and the bridge between. Tamsin's engineered blood makes her the bridge, if she can learn to sing. Beat: passing of the torch, grief foretold.

chapters.title: Learning the Song
chapters.summary: POV Merrin. Merrin trains Tamsin's untrained voice while Sef harmonizes the fae line. Tamsin, who has never been allowed to want anything, discovers joy in music. Beat: tenderness and hope amid the march of war.

chapters.title: Marrowgate Burns
chapters.summary: POV Brannoc. Word arrives: Corvane has sacked Marrowgate as punishment for harboring them. Survivors stream into the mountains. The abstract war becomes faces and ash. Beat: rage and responsibility.

chapters.title: The Free Cities' Council
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. The remaining free cities meet in emergency council; Tamsin pleads for faith in the covenant while generals argue for surrender or hopeless battle. She wins a fragile promise: hold the passes for one moon's turn. Beat: reluctant leadership accepted.

chapters.title: Sef Taken
chapters.summary: POV Sef. Inquisitors raid the camp and seize Sef, whose blood Corvane needs to corrupt the covenant for his own use. The company's guilt and fury nearly tear them apart. Beat: the cost of the mission made flesh.

chapters.title: Into Corvane's Camp
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Against all counsel, Tamsin infiltrates the army's camp using her knowledge of supply roads and her forgotten face. She finds Sef caged and learns Corvane plans to sing a counter-choir at the Deepwell itself. Beat: courage sharpened to a blade's edge.

chapters.title: The Rescue That Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV Merrin. The rescue goes wrong; Aldous anticipated her. Tamsin escapes with Sef only because Merrin gives himself up as a decoy. Beat: sacrifice, and the terror of leaving someone behind.

chapters.title: The Counter-Song
chapters.summary: POV Aldous. Corvane rehearses his corrupted choir with captured fae voices, including Merrin's coerced tenor. Aldous, watching Tamsin's escape succeed, feels the first crack in his certainty. Beat: villain's doubt seeded.

chapters.title: Rallying the Passes
chapters.summary: POV Brannoc. The company scatters word through every smuggler road: hold the passes, buy the singers time. Smugglers, villagers, and deserters form an unlikely host. Beat: ordinary people choosing to stand.

chapters.title: Wren's Last Rite
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Dying, Wren performs the rite that will keep the Deepwell open long enough for the true Choir, spending her final strength. Her death steadies the company rather than breaking it. Beat: mourning transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Moon Turns
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. The deadline arrives. Armies converge on the mountain; the Ash Queen's host descends to watch whether humans honor the bargain. Tamsin stands at the Deepwell with Sef beside her and no third voice. Beat: the darkest hour.

chapters.title: Aldous Chooses
chapters.summary: POV Aldous. At the Deepwell's mouth, Aldous confronts Tamsin one last time — and instead of killing her, he takes up the mortal line of the song himself, buying her the opening bars with his life. Beat: redemption purchased at full price.

chapters.title: The Choir Reforged
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Tamsin sings the bridge-line, her poisoned blood burning through her veins as the covenant takes hold; Sef carries the fae line; freed captives join from Corvane's own choir. The Deepwell blazes with joined voices. Beat: climax — transcendence through agony.

chapters.title: Corvane's Silence
chapters.summary: POV Merrin. The covenant restored, Corvane's counter-song unravels mid-note; his stolen fae voices reclaim themselves and abandon him. His army breaks as the mountain itself turns hostile. Beat: tyrant undone by the voices he stole.

chapters.title: After the Song
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Tamsin wakes changed — her blood no longer poison but part of the covenant, her hearing forever attuned to both realms. The cost: she can never again live fully in either world. Beat: bittersweet victory.

chapters.title: Terms of Peace
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. At the negotiating fire between the free cities and the Ash Queen, Tamsin serves as translator and taster of intentions, reading truth where others hear only words. The accord holds because both sides trust her tongue. Beat: her strange gifts finally honored.

chapters.title: What Merrin Rebuilt
chapters.summary: POV Merrin. Merrin founds a new conservatory in ruined Marrowgate, teaching human and fae children the same songs. He asks Tamsin to stay; she cannot yet answer. Beat: love offered without pressure.

chapters.title: The Road Not Closed
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Tamsin walks the Thornfell passes one last time as a courier, mapping the new crossings between realms. She buries Wren's ashes and Aldous's signet together at the tollhouse. Beat: laying ghosts to rest.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. She returns to Marrowgate not as a weapon or a fugitive but as herself, greeted by name at the gate by Brannoc, Sef, and the conservatory's students. For the first time, a door opens because someone wanted her there. Beat: belonging earned and received.

chapters.title: The First Lesson
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. In the conservatory's hall, Tamsin teaches a class of mixed children to listen for the second voice beneath the first — the skill that saved everything. Merrin watches from the doorway. Beat: legacy beginning.

chapters.title: Felix and the Choir
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin, years later. Framing revelation: 'Felix' was the dying stranger's name, and the story we've read is the ballad the children now sing about him and the taster who finished his song. Tamsin adds a final verse naming everyone who stood with her. Beat: closure — grief, gratitude, and song enduring.
